Subject: Dedicated GPU capacity architecture review — quick ask

Hi Olivia / Helio infra team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As discussed, we'd like to set up a 60–75 minute technical deep-dive to align on: pool sizing, autoscaling behavior, and host isolation/fallback strategies for your Dedicated deployment. Goal: land on a recommended pool topology and a small set of runbook actions for burst scenarios.

Proposed agenda (draft):
- 5m intros and goals
- 15m current workload & SLO expectations (Helio input)
- 25m recommended pool sizing & autoscale policy (Redwood to present)
- 15m isolation/fallback options and testing cadence
- 10m action items + next steps

Please share any additional items to add. Are you available next week on either:
- Tue 22 Dec, 10:00–11:15 PT or
- Wed 23 Dec, 13:00–14:15 PT

If those don't work, propose two slots and we'll coordinate. I can circulate a short pre-read and the current usage snapshot ahead of time.

Thanks,
Jonas
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.ai

Attachments: (none in this message)

We do have a couple asks before we lock time:
- Can you send a 1–2 page pre-read that calls out the recommended inputs you need from us?
- Please include a sizing rationale checklist (example: 95th pct token throughput, cold-start windows, KV cache hit assumptions).

Also, can we limit attendees to the core infra folks + 1 solutions engineer from Redwood? We'll pull in others as needed for runbook sign-off.

Olivia — thanks. Agree on a small core group. Wed 23 Dec 13:00 PT is locked for now (I’ll send a calendar invite after you confirm names).

I attached a short pre-read and a one-page sizing checklist (both attached). Pre-read includes:
- current assumptions we used to size pools for similar customers
- trade-offs for eager vs conservative autoscale policies
- isolation strategies (tenant vs pool-level, warm-standby rearrangements)
- a list of telemetry we need from Helio to finalize numbers

Action items for Helio before the meeting:
1) Share a 24h token-by-minute sample, and a 72h spike sample if available (heliotech-current-usage.csv).
2) Confirm SLOs (p99 latency target, acceptable tail latency under bursts).
3) Point contact for runbook ownership (name + email).

If anything in the pre-read is unclear, flag it and we’ll adjust before Wed.

Jonas

Attachments: 20261220-HelioTech-capacity-pre-read.pdf, heliotech-current-usage.csv
